key_insight: In CFD simulations at L/D = 5 and pressure drops above 0.2 MPa, sharp-edged inlets showed strong cavitation while chamfered inlets showed cavitation inception.
engineering_relevance: Inlet geometry and orifice length-to-diameter ratio are important design considerations for controlling cavitation and hydraulic flip in liquid injectors.
method: CFD using k–ω SST turbulence, Zwart–Gerber–Belamri cavitation, and Volume of Fluid models.
Compared sharp-edged and chamfered water-injector inlets.
Studied pressure drops of 0.07–0.59 MPa and L/D ratios of 2, 5, and 10.
evidence_signal: Volumetric flow predictions were validated against existing experiments, and hydraulic flip at L/D = 5 and 0.59 MPa for the sharp-edged inlet agreed with prior experimental findings.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation errors, limiting assessment of predictive accuracy beyond the reported agreement.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Flow and Cavitation in Single-Liquid Injectors with Sharp-Edged and Chamfered Orifice Inlets
